searchText: We're about to push another fix There was a mistake in the previous PR A lot of people are about to get slashed, my node has ~3k attester slashings in the op pool, and there are lots in the recent blocks (from slot 75000 up) do we know by what time the network is expected to stabilize? (deleted previous message, realised I was double counting slashings from blocks at skipped slots) 817 validators have been slashed so far, by my count (that's total, but there were very few slashed until recently): https://gist.github.com/michaelsproul/6762223aea4840a901f5290aa1065ca6 Most of the validators are hosted by prysmatic labs. We are working on a summary report now. Thanks <@!602753420033785856> for the heads up! On the bright side, some lucky proposers out there will be getting rich! what’s the cause for the slashings and how could that be avoided by the user? <@602753420033785856> it looks like we can’t sync our nodes for the explorer until the network stabilizes > what’s the cause for the slashings and how could that be avoided by the user? <@!602753420033785856> <@!97774605351010304> this was a prylabs infra oversight, we are drafting a blog post on it now. Will share it with the community on monday. Most of the users didnt get slashed because there's local protection DB on by default thanks <@363800010518822915> the network was down but doesn’t look too bad to me if those slashings could have been avoided. also, what’s the incentives in this case to have a better client diversification in the network if the penalties are small? maybe your post can cover these q‘s 😅 We'll definitely cover them! Also if this was mainnet, I'd imagine most prysm validators would already have migrated to lh/teku/nimbus/lodestar The penalties with quadratic leak will get steeper How fast is migration possible? Like are there any time constraints by design to switch clients? <@!707707212184944702> I think it could be quite fast if you keep a beacon node for a second client running in sync with your Eth1 node without running its validator. If the first client gets into trouble you shut it off and fire up the validator for the second client. Time constraint is that you'd have to be careful not to get slashed by making sure the validator for the second client isn't acting in the same epoch as the first client. So worst case ~6.5 mins? If the second client has slashing protection you wouldn't need to worry. Ok, that sounds reasonable. Are you keeping a beacon node for a second client running? Not right now. I tried a few scenarios with Prysm, Lighthouse, and Teku running on the same instance. My general setup guides for those clients are here (https://medium.com/@SomerEsat) if you want to set them up yourself. Haven’t tried Lodestar or Nimbus at all, yet, but I’m going to write guides for them too, and after that I’ll explore additional scenarios. > That has been a very interesting test of the various tools. eth2stats is showing nodes as behind even though their head slot matches what it reports a current slot (I suspect because there are some Prsym nodes still off in the future). Beaconcha.in and beaconscan have both had similar problems. <@340345049063882753> this is weird, the coloring of the nodes is done by interval from local browser clock, it should not have been affected by this. the whole network could stop and the top slot counter would go on, not caring one bit about our tears of sadness :p like now 😢 I don't want to live in a world where machines are ambivalent to my tears. > Is anyone monitoring eth1 data votes? > I'm curious about how quickly we are reaching consensus on eth1 <@!399309815517544451> This might not be top priority right now, but here's my analysis for future reference: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/issues/2018 To eth2 devs and researchers, i have been wondering, at the time of finality difficulty due to participation rate drop, why we have to wait for the participation picking up, many cases very long time. Should there be a way to rescue, quickly, a emergency method? Treating the network as a battle ground, and staking token as army, we should have reserve stakes, just like reserve army, ready at hand, and put into fighting at emergency situation like this. One of the short coming of staking is that, once deposit is made, validators are activated, tokens must be put in use, they cannot be in standby state, otherwise, penalty will be imposed. Can we add a reserve state, for some tokens are only placed into reserve state, only put into use in the emergency situation like this. Those reserve stakes / token won't be count into total deposit, won't be calculated in participation rate. <@387720149345763329> what you're proposing is fundamentally opposed to the principle of decentralization. There is no god mode switch in eth2 and there are good reasons for this. reserve stakes could also be decentrlized if you have done stock trading, you'll know traders always have reserve cash, only put in use in rare cases. those cash will be returned to reserve when the situations are over. Now i want to deposit more to help the situation, but that won't help. cause new deposit takes hours to be activated, and no finality, no new validator will be activated, thus partitipation rate can't go up. Couple of lighthouse and prysm testnets died this way. <@!291925846556540928> <@!573787335796326400> <@!311971895828283393> <@!361447803194441738> <@387720149345763329> How would reserve stakes help? Existing stakes can be transferred to working clients quite easily. The problem is that the network is so messed up it doesn't help. Reserve stakes does not solve this. "Existing stakes can be transferred to working clients quite easily. " -- it is not happening keystores / validator/ stakes are not multi-clients compatible this time. I've been trying to do swap between lighthouse and prysm, IMPOSSIBLE. Import from launchpad cli keystore to prysm and also to lighthouse (ex.). Keep your preferred client running and only the beacon chain of your backup client. If the first client goes down, startup the validator of your backup client and its quick because the beacon chain is already synced. launchpad can't do batch deposit. For 1000 copy stake, you have to click 1000 confirmation button ... ~12.8 million $? 🤷‍♂️ 1000*32=32k eth For someone who thinks transferring keys is IMPOSSIBLE... that is 1000 transactions, for each transaction, metamask ask for confirmation i've raised the issue weeks before, at the launch so i used lighthouse batch deposit transferring key is only possible / practical for a few keys, not for many keys From lighthouse to prysm? if you have your mnemonic you could do an account recover in prysm. All keys in one shot. But anway I think i'm in over my head here. you were not involved in my discussion wsith lighthouse and prysm. not possible they don't have tools <@387720149345763329> take a look at the ethdo tool, you can do all of this with it not i asked <@!144468805697929216> already We'll, this seems like a much easier problem to solve than changing the protocol. yes but please give me the tools seems like i'm the only one went through the trouble - making batch deposit and trying to convert keys to different clients I've read keys from the Launchpad, from LH and from ethdo into Teku, no problems. yes. no prblem. however, not for large number of keys can't do batch deposit in launchapad, again That's a different issue entirely. so there you go, large number of keys cannot switch to different client, and prysm client had problem I really don't understand. I'm perfectly able to transfer large numbers of keys from other clients into Teku. I can't speak for other clients, but this actually works. Prysm put support for standard key stores in place just before Medalla aiui. they changed it No they didn't, you can batch import arbitrary numbers of keystore files into prysm, just did it today. launchpad right? Doesn't matter where they come from, standard keystore format it matters. lighthouse also uses standard keystore format looks like all clients use the same standard both teams thought they can import other teams' key files, both were wrong Maybe we should move this discussion to the ethstaker discord to keep this channel for r&d discussions ok Has anyone looked at the chain data to see if we have partitioning/forks? From eth2stats.io it looks like there's a few separate groups of clients moving the chain head forward.

excerpts.author: bobcat6146
excerpts.content:
To eth2 devs and researchers, 

i have been wondering, at the time of finality difficulty due to participation rate drop, why we have to wait for the participation picking up, many cases very long time. Should there be a way to rescue, quickly, a emergency method?

Treating the network as a battle ground, and staking token as army, we should have reserve stakes, just like reserve army, ready at hand, and put into fighting at emergency situation like this.

One of the short coming of staking is that, once deposit is made, validators are activated, tokens must be put in use, they cannot be in standby state, otherwise, penalty will be imposed. Can we add a reserve state, for some tokens are only placed into reserve state, only put into use in the emergency situation like this. Those reserve stakes / token won't be count into total deposit, won't be calculated in participation rate.
